entries.title: Family menu and a calmer dashboard

items.text: A small grid button now opens a list of the other HOP apps, starting with HOP ID, so you can jump to them without scrolling to the footer. Before, the top bar had no shortcut to the other apps. Once you are signed in, the same list is in the sidebar of your dashboard instead.

An announcement from the site owner can now appear as a card at the top of your dashboard, with a Close button. A closed announcement stays hidden for a week. When there is no announcement, nothing is shown and no empty space is left. This gives every HOP dashboard a place for news.

The line "Part of Hop Easy Link" is now the last line at the bottom of the sidebar, and the sidebar on a phone reaches the bottom of the screen. Before, the line only existed in the public page footer, so it was missing from the dashboard.

If you are signed in, the PayHop logo and the Back button on a page that does not exist now take you to your dashboard instead of the public home page. Visitors who are not signed in still go to the home page. People signed in kept landing on the public page and had to find their way back.
If you are signed in, these pages now open inside your dashboard, with the sidebar around them, so there is always a way back. Visitors and search engines still see them as public pages.

items.where: Top bar and home page on phones
items.text: On phones 360 to 390 pixels wide the top bar no longer runs past the right edge in any of the nine languages: on the narrowest screens it shows the logo alone, the language button shows only its globe, and the menus open fully on the screen. The table of payment formats on the home page now scrolls inside its own box instead of making the whole page wider. Reported by the site owner.

The changelog now lists one plain-language entry per release, grouped as added, changed, fixed and so on, with a Technical details link to the full notes. Before, it listed raw code changes, which most people could not read. The page is written from this file and checked by the automatic tests.

A mistyped address now answers "not found" properly instead of showing the app as if the page existed. Search engines and link checkers no longer take such addresses for real pages. Addresses PayHop does own are unchanged.

The automatic tests now run on Windows too, and a test loads the finished app in a real browser and fails on a blank page or an error. Another test keeps the public pages identical for every visitor language, which is why they can be stored safely by shared caches. Nothing changes on screen.

items.where: Payment QR and Split a bill
items.text: You can now try the app without any payment details: "Try with sample data" fills the generator and "Load an example bill" fills the bill splitter. A sample is clearly marked "SAMPLE: not a real account. Do not pay." on the code and on the downloaded picture, and the code itself cannot be paid, so nobody can send money to a made-up account by mistake. Only the SEPA euro format has a sample, because it is the only one with an example that belongs to nobody.

Your choice of light or dark and of language is now remembered across the HOP apps, so you do not have to pick it again in each one. It is read before the page appears, so the page does not flash the wrong theme.
Search engines and readers without scripts now get the real first screen of each page, with the same top bar, heading and look as the app, instead of a hidden block of text.
PayHop now remembers a language only when you pick one, instead of every time a page loads.

Opening PayHop from the HOP ID launcher now lands you on your account page, already signed in, and the Sign in button on any page brings you back to that page. Another account signing in after you sign out sees nothing of yours.

entries.title: First release
entries.summary: The first release: payment QR codes and a bill splitter that run in your browser, with accounts that can keep payment methods and bills, part of the HOP family.

items.text: Make a payment QR code for PayPal.me, Cash App, Venmo, Solana Pay, UPI, EPC SEPA, PromptPay and VietQR. The receiver name is required, shown next to the code and printed under it, and a tick is needed before download, so a wrong code is less likely to be paid. Every format says it has not been tested in a wallet yet, because that is true.
Add who was there, what each item cost and who shared it; taxes and tips are spread by what each person ordered and the shares add up exactly.

Signed in with your HOP ID, you can keep up to 20 payment methods and the last 200 bills. They are stored encrypted, only when you tick a box for each one, and you can delete one or all at any time. Without that choice nothing is saved.

English, Chinese, German, Indonesian, Japanese, Portuguese, Spanish, French and Russian, light and dark, with a calm static page for people who prefer reduced motion. It works offline after the first visit.
Each page has its own address for search engines, the signed-in page is kept out of search results, and the privacy and terms pages say plainly what is stored.
The receiver name printed on the picture is cut at a whole character, never in the middle of an emoji.
